observation: All earlier what-if physics (P0, P4b, P0c) lower predictions of degraded inputs; none lifts predictions, and long-life cells stay underpredicted (~ -1000 cycles). On split-2021 train cells Spearman(last-observed SOH, log EOL) = 0.921, yet frozen ZN-E010 changes its prediction by only +18 cycles on average for a +15% capacity ramp and violates the mirror rule P0u on 14.7% of val samples. SOH lower bounds were checked and rejected as too weak (loss.md §4.6).
primary_hypothesis: The label-free rule 'more remaining capacity cannot mean a shorter life' (P0u), enforced on improved what-ifs x(1 + alpha r_n), makes predictions respond upward to higher capacity, lowering the held-out P0u violation >= 50% vs ZN-E010 and lifting long-life predictions: >1000-cycle bias smaller than ZN-E010's -970 and KEEP under §7 vs ZN-E010.
question_inherited: Does an upward-correcting capacity physics rule reduce the long-life underprediction that downward rules could not?
unresolved_from_reference: Whether ZN-E010's weak capacity sensitivity is the reason long-life (high-SOH) cells are underpredicted.
why_this_experiment: User request A7-ZN (new physics). P0u is newly registered in loss.md §4.6 with Zn-ion evidence; it is the only label-free capacity rule that corrects upward.
modification: Loss only: L = RelativeHuber_0.15 + lambda * mean ReLU(sg[f(x)] - f(x~)), x~_{n,Q,dis} = x_{n,Q,dis} (1 + alpha r_n) on observed cycles, alpha ~ U(0, 0.150), r_n = clip((n-10)/90,0,1); lambda = 0.5 x median gradient ratio (unsigned calibration). Model and training identical to ZN-E010.
changed_components: Objective: added label-free P0u capacity-improvement physics term (T008).
held_constant_components: Frozen ZN-E010 architecture (98,113 params, GELU, anchored fade encoder), Relative Huber delta 0.15 main loss, Adam lr 5e-4, batch 128, seed 2021, split 2021, A2-ZN epochs, checkpoint rule, data.
controlled_variables: Training seed 2021, split 2021, minimum 5 / maximum 100 epochs, patience 5 after epoch 5, diagnostics every 50 steps; lambda2 never tuned on validation.
expected_evidence: MAPE/Acc@15/RMSE/DB-MAPE vs ZN-E010; held-out P0u violation vs 0.147; >1000 and 500-1000 bias vs ZN-E010; prediction change for a +15% capacity ramp; lambda, R, cosine, active fraction; gradient gate.
rejection_condition: Primary rule (program.md §7, vs frozen reference ZN-E010 MAPE 0.3325 / RMSE 425.0 / Acc@15 0.3665 / DB-MAPE 0.3325). KEEP iff [A: MAPE <= 0.3245 AND RMSE <= 435.0] OR [B: RMSE <= 404.0 AND MAPE <= 0.3355] OR [C: Acc@15 >= 0.3865 AND MAPE <= 0.3355 AND RMSE <= 435.0], AND Acc@15 >= 0.3365 (A/B) AND DB-MAPE <= 0.3425 AND gradient gate PASS AND loss balance PASS or SATISFIED (loss.md §5.3) AND prediction SD >= 10% of target SD; otherwise DISCARD. Physics claim only if the held-out P0u violation falls vs ZN-E010 (0.147) and accuracy does not get worse.
minimum_evidence_requirements: At least five complete epochs; finite MAPE, Acc@15, MAE, and RMSE from one checkpoint; sample and unique-cell counts for every domain; gradient, update, activation, prediction, mask, and compute diagnostics.
required_diagnostics: Epoch learning curve; selected and minimum-MAPE epochs; cycle_stem, residual_blocks, fade_encoder, inter_summary and head gradients and updates; activation health; prediction spread and bias; prefix, domain and EOL errors; padding sensitivity; parameters, memory, time, throughput. Loss balance: lambda2, R_j median, cosine, active fraction (loss.md §5.3).

architecture_addendum.evidence: Phase-2 loss experiment on the frozen ZN-E010 architecture
architecture_addendum.shapes: [B,100,3,300] -> ResConv [B,100,64] (h_t) -> u_t=[h_t, h_t-h_1] [B,100,128] -> Linear 128->64, GELU, Linear 64->64, +h_t -> g_t [B,100,64] * mask -> masked summary [B,192] -> Linear [B,64] -> GELU -> Linear [B,1]
